CRI / NOREPINEPHRINE

Norepinephrine CRI

Uses the shared species and weight above. Workbook profiles & clinical references.

Best use: Titrate to blood pressure and perfusion after reassessing volume status; monitor the catheter site closely. Veterinary reference.

Prepare an infusion

Start at 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min; titrate to blood-pressure response.

Access · workbook guardrails, not validated maximums

Target-rate mode calculates concentration for a NEW preparation at the selected dose. Known-concentration mode lets you enter the concentration of a prepared syringe. Run time is calculated. Do not remake an existing syringe whenever the dose changes: keep its concentration fixed and titrate its pump rate. Duration is nominal before priming/discard.

Patient / cage: ____________________

Titrate to the veterinarian’s prescribed BP/perfusion goal. Rows are calculation references, not instructions for dose increments or timing; the last row is not a maximum dose. Rates are rounded. Reprint if patient weight or preparation concentration changes.

Best practice · syringe-pump setup

Use a compatible syringe pump for a diluted, titratable infusion; verify syringe brand/size, line setup and pump performance at the chosen rate. Keep the prepared concentration fixed when titrating an existing syringe.

Our preparation defaults: concentration-based mode, 0.05 mcg/kg/min, 15 mcg/mL and 12 mL final. These are local workflow preferences, not universal veterinary standards. A canine clinical pilot study used patient-specific dilution so 0.1 mcg/kg/min initially ran at 1 mL/hr; it did not establish an optimal syringe size or flow rate. Target-pump-rate preparation remains available as an alternative; in concentration-based mode, pump rate and run time are calculated from the patient’s weight and selected dose. Lyons, Hess & Silverstein, 2025.

Connect the extension set close to the catheter to limit delivery delay; account for priming and residual volume. Prime/purge before connecting to the patient. Estimated duration is before priming/discard and changes whenever the pump rate changes. AAHA 2024 · administration guidance · Veterinary syringe-pump manual · use your own model’s instructions.

Worked math

More info · concentration reference

Norepinephrine concentration

Assumed stock: 1 mg/mL = 1,000 mcg/mL norepinephrine base. Verify the actual vial. Diluent: D5W per workbook; confirm product compatibility and stability.

Workbook comparison options: 8, 16, 32 and 64 mcg/mL. Peripheral 16 / central 64 mcg/mL are retained workbook guardrails, not validated veterinary maximums. No universal veterinary maximum was substantiated in the reviewed veterinary sources.

A veterinary case series reports peripheral vasopressor extravasation injury and supports central access when feasible and consideration of lower concentrations. Concentration alone does not establish line safety.

Practice source

Merck Veterinary Manual · veterinary clinical reference. Best-use wording is a clinical summary, not a complete treatment protocol.

Veterinary sources

  • Lathroum et al., JVECC 2024: peripheral vasopressor extravasation in 3 dogs — does not establish a maximum concentration.
